## Line 215

```plato

    //==
    // # Elementary transforms
    //
    // The single-purpose transforms of `transforms.types.plato` — translation,
    // scaling, reflection, and the about-a-centre forms. Each one names what it
    // does instead of hiding it in a matrix, and each converts into the affine
    // transform of its dimension (its `IAffine2D` / `IAffine3D` obligation), which
    // is where transforms of different kinds are composed.

    //==
    // Translations — a rigid shift. A translation moves positions but not
    // displacements, so its action on a vector is the identity.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Translation_(geometry)

    // The translation as an affine map (identity linear part).
    AffineTransform2D(t: Translation2D): AffineTransform2D
        => AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(t.Vector));
```

## Line 402

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/transforms.library.plato, line 402](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/transforms.library.plato#L402).

```plato

    //==
    // Reflections — the mirror in a line (2D) or a plane (3D). A reflection is
    // its own inverse, and no reflection is the identity map, so there is no
    // Identity static here. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reflection_(mathematics)

    // The mirror as an affine map: translate the mirror's origin to the world
    // origin, reflect the basis, translate back. The linear rows are the images
    // of the world axes, so the reflection formula is not restated.
    AffineTransform2D(r: Reflection2D): AffineTransform2D {
        var o = r.Origin.PositionVector;
        var n = Vector2D(-r.Direction.Vector.Y, r.Direction.Vector.X);
        var x = Vector2D(1.0, 0.0).Reflect(n);
        var y = Vector2D(0.0, 1.0).Reflect(n);
        var linear = AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2(
            Number2(x.X, x.Y),
            Number2(y.X, y.Y),
            Number2(0.0, 0.0)));
        return AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(-o))
            .Compose(linear)
            .Compose(AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateTranslation(o)));
    }
```

    //==
    // About-a-centre transforms — a rotation or a scaling conjugated by the
    // translation of its centre. The linear part is unaffected by the centre, so
    // their action on displacements is the centre-free one.

    // The rotation about the centre as an affine map.
    AffineTransform2D(r: RotationAbout2D): AffineTransform2D
        => AffineTransform2D(Matrix3x2.CreateRotation(r.Rotation.Angle, r.Center));
